text:
Morgan Barron was a sixth-round pick, a checking forward with 83 points in 321 career games, and he is suddenly on a four-game point streak (3 goals, 2 assists) for a Jets team that keeps winning. Thirteen points in 26 games puts him near a league-average scoring rate in 14.7 minutes a night, with 63 hits and 28 blocked shots alongside.

The chances don't back the scoring. His 6 goals come on 3.7 expected, a 16.7% shooting rate when our estimate of his true rate is 13.4%, and Winnipeg has scored 6.5 more goals than expected with him on the ice. At 5v5 the Jets get only 40% of the expected goals when he plays.

That's the role, not a flaw. He kills penalties, blocks shots and soaks up hard minutes, the same profile as Michael McCarron or Mark Kastelic. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 59% of his shots coming off the rush last season, so his goals arrive in transition. Enjoy the streak; the bounces are doing a lot of it.
headline: Barron is scoring like a top-six winger
